---
title: "the model lifecycle"
---

## the loop

- define → prepare data → train → validate → release → monitor → improve or retire
- feedback can send you back to the problem definition or data, rather than always leading to retraining [aws lifecycle overview](https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/mlops/)

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0"}

| stage | what to do | what to keep |
|---|---|---|
| define | specify the user, prediction time, target, and success metric | task definition and baseline |
| prepare | check data quality; choose splits that reflect intended use | data version, schema, split rules |
| train | fit preprocessing and candidates on training data | code, parameters, environment |
| validate | compare candidates and error patterns; freeze choices before final testing | evaluation report and release criteria |
| release | package the pipeline; test predictions in the target environment | versioned artifact and rollback plan |
| monitor | track service health and model quality when outcomes arrive | logs, metrics, alerts, owner |
| improve / retire | investigate changes; validate replacements or stop an obsolete system | decision and version history |

:::

## keep evaluation honest

- **training:** learn preprocessing and model parameters
- **validation / cross-validation:** choose features, hyperparameters, thresholds, and models
- **test:** estimate final performance after those choices are fixed; repeatedly tuning to it turns it into validation data
- fit transformations within training folds. a pipeline helps prevent preprocessing leakage, but cannot fix a leaked target or an inappropriate split [scikit-learn pitfalls](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html)
- random row splits suit the independent synthetic example below; use group or time-aware splits when observations share entities or deployment predicts the future [model selection guide](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/model_selection.html)

## try it locally

- goal: run a small binary-classification experiment, save its preprocessing and model together, and verify reloaded predictions
- [download the example script](../../examples/lifecycle_demo.py) into an empty project folder
- these commands assume a unix-like shell and an installed `python3`:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install scikit-learn numpy joblib
python lifecycle_demo.py --output artifacts/run-001
python -m pip freeze > requirements-lock.txt
```

- the script makes synthetic data, creates 60/20/20 train/validation/test splits, and compares three logistic-regression settings against a constant-probability baseline using validation roc auc
- it selects the best validation candidate, evaluates it on the held-out test set, and saves `pipeline.joblib` plus `run.json`
- the run record contains metrics, settings, split sizes, a dataset fingerprint, and package versions; commit the script and dependency file, and record the commit id alongside the run
- repeated runs need a new output folder, such as `artifacts/run-002`. keep the same environment when comparing reproducibility

```python
# the central pattern used in the downloadable script
model = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(C=1.0))
model.fit(x_train, y_train)  # the scaler sees training data only
probabilities = model.predict_proba(x_val)[:, 1]
joblib.dump(model, "pipeline.joblib")
```

- saving a pipeline is local packaging, not deployment; the example stops before serving or production monitoring
- retain compatible dependencies and load only trusted model files; pickle-based formats such as joblib can execute code when loaded [model persistence guide](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/model_persistence.html)

## turn the exercise into a workflow

- add a test for input shape and invalid values, then a repeatable batch prediction command
- automate the training smoke test in ci; keep model-quality checks separate from code checks
- before releasing, define acceptable performance, service requirements, and how to restore the previous version
- after releasing, monitor input quality and service failures immediately; measure predictive quality as labels arrive
- drift is a cue to investigate. validate a retrained model before replacing the current one [google’s validation and automation guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/mlops-continuous-delivery-and-automation-pipelines-in-machine-learning)
